newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major sets plans to boost share ownership.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major sets plans to boost share ownership.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Friday proposed a series of measures to increase ownership of shares, boost pension schemes and help small businesses.
Major told a news conference that the measures would give Britons a greater share in the country's prosperity.
"Our aim is for everyone to have a Peoples' Share in our enterprise economy," he said, adding this would be a core theme of the ruling Conservatives' manifesto at the coming election.
Major made the following specific proposals:
-- Inland Revenue tax rules will be relaxed to allow companies to top up employees' investment in shares with free shares from the company.
He said he wanted this initiative, called Sharematch, to become a normal part of employment packages.
-- Rules will be eased to allow small businesses to set up personal pension schemes for groups of employees. This will make it cheaper to administer personal pension schemes.
-- Rules will be eased to allow a self-employed person to take his or her pension with them if he or she joins a company.

-- Anyone who has invested extra savings alongside his or her company pension scheme will be given the chance for the first time to take that part of their pension earlier or later than their main company pension.
-- The uniform business rate, one of the heaviest burdens on small businesses, will be reformed specifically to help the small firms.

-- The government will accelerate deregulation by introducing "sunset provisions" in new legislation. This means many new laws and rules will automatically lapse after a certain period unless the government acts to renew them.
"Conservatives believe that people should share in success through ownership. That's our promise for the future. That's the peoples' share," Major said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7950
